#### 3.4.1. Solving bit-vectors

Z3 mostly uses a bit-blasting approach to deciding bit-vectors. By bit-blasting we refer to a reduction of bit-vector constraints to propositional logic by treating each bit in a bit-vector as a propositional variable. Let us illustrate how bit-vector addition is compiled to a set of clauses. The expression `v + w`, where `v` and `w` are bit-vectors is represented by a vector `out` of output bits. The relation between `v`, `w` and `out` is provided by clauses the encode a ripple-carry adder seen in Figure [2](#fig-bvadd "Bit-vector addition circuit"). The encoding uses an auxiliary vector of *carry bits* that are internal to the adder.
